name: Dan-Gouèta / dan de l'Est, dialecte de Gouèta
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 4 other works consulted do not discuss stress.

catalog_quote: Le dan-gouèta a cinq tonèmes simples, essentiellement réalisés comme tons unis: [...] S’y ajoute trois tons modulés: [...] Le ton joue un rôle grammatical très important en dan-gouèta. (p. 10) [...] Les séquences comme bhánŋ́ et glōō sont des pieds, unités intermédiaires entre les syllabes et les mots; leur rôle en dan (comme dans les autres langues du groupe mandé-sud) est prépondérant. (p. 11) [fn. 6] Il est évident que le type de pied qu'on observe dans les langues mandé est différent de celui dans des langues à accent (« le pied métrique »). Le type mandé peut être défini par le terme anglais « featural foot », proposé par Green (2015); en français, on peut traduire ce terme par « pied caractéristique ».
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress
sweep_summary: Dan (dann1241, Mande) is not in the catalog. Both target items are the same work, Bolli's 1975/1976 'Etude prosodique du dan (blossé)' (47 pp., ILA-SIL Abidjan): print-only (BnF ark:/12148/cb366704312; SUDOC 019012977; SIL archive id 15398 is a dead link), no digital copy anywhere; contemporary literature (Vydrin & Roberts 2019) files it as the early 'prosody' study beside Flik 1977 on tone, so it most likely concerns tone, priority medium. Best first-hand statement read: Vydrin 2021, Mandenkan 64 grammar sketch of Eastern Dan (open access, saved) — five level tonemes plus three falling tones, heavy grammatical tone, and a 'featural foot' explicitly contrasted with the metrical foot of accent languages; no stress rule is stated. Vydrin 2016 (tonal inflection, HAL) and Akinlabi, Ahoua & Gondo 2022 (SPiL Plus, open) agree: tone only, no word stress. Unread: Flik 1977 (De Gruyter, paywalled), Bearth & Zemp 1967 (print), Person/Bolli/Flik 1975 SIL microfiche, Makeeva 2012 and Gondo 2014/2016 theses (previously marked not located).

new_statements.quote: Le dan-gouèta a cinq tonèmes simples, essentiellement réalisés comme tons unis [...] S’y ajoute trois tons modulés [...] Le ton joue un rôle grammatical très important en dan-gouèta. (p. 10) [...] Les séquences comme bhánŋ́ et glōō sont des pieds, unités intermédiaires entre les syllabes et les mots ; leur rôle en dan (comme dans les autres langues du groupe mandé-sud) est prépondérant. (p. 11) [fn. 6:] Il est évident que le type de pied qu'on observe dans les langues mandé est différent de celui dans des langues à accent (« le pied métrique »). Le type mandé peut être défini par le terme anglais « featural foot », proposé par Green (2015) ; en français, on peut traduire ce terme par « pied caractéristique ».
new_statements.translation: Dan-Gouèta has five simple tonemes, realised essentially as level tones [...] To these are added three contour tones [...] Tone plays a very important grammatical role in Dan-Gouèta. (p. 10) [...] Sequences such as bhánŋ́ and glōō are feet, units intermediate between syllables and words; their role in Dan (as in the other languages of the South Mande group) is preponderant. (p. 11) [fn. 6:] It is evident that the type of foot observed in the Mande languages is different from that found in accent languages ('the metric foot'). The Mande type can be defined by the English term 'featural foot', proposed by Green (2015); in French one may translate this term as 'pied caractéristique'.

new_statements.rule_in_words: No rule for word stress is given. Dan is described as a five-level-tone language (plus three contour tones) with a heavy grammatical use of tone; the word is organised into 'featural' feet (light V/CV, heavy CVV/CVŋ, extra-heavy CVVV/CVVŋ) defined by nasal harmony, tone-combination and vowel-combination restrictions, not by prominence. The only remark bearing on accent is fn. 6, which distinguishes this Mande foot from the metric foot of accent languages. Word stress is neither located nor explicitly denied.
new_statements.domain_note: Description of the Gouèta (Gwɛɛtaa) dialect of Eastern Dan, Côte d'Ivoire; tone domain is the syllable, foot is the rhythmic unit; most words are one foot. Other opened sources (Vydrin 2016; Roberts & Vydrin 2019; Makeeva 2012 avtoreferat on Kla-Dan; Griffes & Welmers 1960 on Liberian Gio; Akinlabi, Ahoua & Gondo 2022 on Dan-Gblewo) are equally silent on stress.
new_statements.identity_note: Glottolog 5.1 'Dan' (dann1241, ISO daf) subsumes as dialects Eastern Dan (east2794) incl. Gweetaawu (gwee1242), Nuclear Dan (nucl1770, ISO dnj), Kla-Dan (klad1234, ISO lda), Lower Gio (lowe1406) etc. The quoted source describes the Gouèta/Gwɛɛtaa dialect of Eastern Dan (Côte d'Ivoire). Other sources examined cover Kla-Dan (Makeeva 2012), Liberian Gio (Griffes & Welmers 1960), Dan-Gblewo (Akinlabi, Ahoua & Gondo 2022), Santa (Bearth & Zemp 1967) and Blossé (Bolli & Flik 1975; Bolli 1976); all fall within dann1241.

new_statements.quote: Le dan-gouèta a cinq tonèmes simples, essentiellement réalisés comme tons unis : 1) extra-haut : ka̋a ‘gale’ ; 2) haut : káa ‘vous’ ; 3) moyen : kāa ‘vous’ ; 4) bas : kàa ‘gratter’ ; 5) extra-bas : kȁa ‘roseau’. S’y ajoute trois tons modulés [...] Il est évident que le type de pied qu'on observe dans les langues mandé est différent de celui dans des langues à accent (« le pied métrique »). Le type mandé peut être défini par le terme anglais « featural foot », proposé par Green (2015) ; en français, on peut traduire ce terme par « pied caractéristique ».
new_statements.translation: Dan-Gouèta has five simple tonemes, essentially realised as level tones: 1) extra-high, 2) high, 3) mid, 4) low, 5) extra-low. Three modulated (falling) tones are added to these [...] It is evident that the type of foot observed in the Mande languages is different from that of accent languages ('the metrical foot'). The Mande type can be defined by the English term 'featural foot' proposed by Green (2015).
new_statements.citation: Vydrin, Valentin (2021). Esquisse de grammaire du dan de l'Est (dialecte de Gouèta). Mandenkan 64: 3-80. doi:10.4000/mandenkan.2406
new_statements.locator: §2.2 Tons, p. 10 (paragraph 20) and §2.3 L'organisation rythmique : pieds, p. 11, footnote 6
new_statements.reading: Eastern Dan is a five-level tone language with no word-stress rule stated anywhere in the phonology of the most recent first-hand grammar sketch; its rhythmic unit is a featural foot that the author explicitly distinguishes from the metrical foot of accent languages. Coding for a stress catalog: no word stress / tone-only (the sketch never posits accent; the only 'accent' mention is the contrast with accent languages).

new_statements.relation_note: The open later edition is the very source of the catalog record (tonal, no stress statement); the 2008 first edition's sketch is by the author's own statement the earlier, shorter version of the same text, so no different stress statement is expected, but the 2008 printing itself was not seen.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Eastern Dan (Gouèta) is described as a five-level tone language (plus three contour tones) whose words are organised into 'featural' feet; the sketch posits no word stress or accent anywhere, and its only mention of accent is the contrast between the Mande foot and the metrical foot of accent languages.
new_statements.secondary_stress: none mentioned (no stress posited at all)
new_statements.exceptions: none; the extra-high-falling contour tone is said to be rare and probably absent from many Eastern Dan dialects outside Gouèta
new_statements.identity_note: Catalog variety: Eastern Dan, Gouèta (Gwɛɛtaa) dialect (Vydrin). Bearth & Zemp 1967 describe the Santa dialect and Bolli 1976 the Blossé (Blowo) dialect, both Western Dan; Vydrine & Kességbeu 2008 / Vydrin 2021 describe Gouèta.

tone_statements.translation: Flik distinguishes three level tones (high, mid, low) and two contour tones [...]. The tone-bearing unit is the syllable (vowel). [...] The most significant addition that must be made is the recognition in Dan-Blo of one more contour tone, the 'high-falling' one. [...] Thus the tonal system of Dan-Blo becomes symmetrical: three level tones and three (corresponding) contour tones: high ~ high-falling, mid ~ mid-falling, low ~ low-falling/assimilated.

sources.citation: Roberts, David & Valentin Vydrin (2019). Tonal oral reading errors in the orthography of Eastern Dan (Côte d'Ivoire). Nordic Journal of African Studies. HAL halshs-02482138 [found in search]
sources.quote: Early linguistic research on Eastern Dan includes a phonology sketch (Bearth and Zemp 1967), and studies of dialect mutual intelligibility (Bolli, Flik, and Bendor-Samuel 1972), prosody (Bolli 1976), tone (Flik 1977), tense-aspect and discourse (Flik 1978).
sources.note: Orthography/reading study; its literature review lists Bolli 1976 as the early study of Dan 'prosody' and Flik 1977 as the tone study, and gives the tone inventory (five level tones, six contours). No word-stress statement.

sources.citation: Vydrin, Valentin (2016). Tonal inflection in Mande languages: The cases of Bamana and Dan-Gwɛɛtaa. In E. L. Palancar & J. L. Léonard (eds.), Tone and Inflection, 83-105. Berlin: De Gruyter. HAL halshs-01287458 [found in search]
sources.quote: The domain of a tone is the syllable. Another important rhythmic unit in Dan is the metric foot (cf. in particular (Vydrin 2010a)): there are numerous restrictions on combinations of tones within this unit (see 3.1.2). There are in Dan light feet (V, CV), heavy feet (CVV, CVŋ, CVVV, CVVŋ, ClVŋ, ClVV) and extraheavy feet (CVVV, CVVŋ). Contextual changes of tones are very few
sources.note: Describes Dan-Gwɛɛtaa as a 5-level-tone language in which the tone-bearing unit is the syllable and the metric foot is the other rhythmic unit; speaks of the foot-initial tone as 'a strong position' but states no stress or accent rule. Consistent with Vydrin 2021.

sources.citation: Makeeva, N. V. 2012. Grammaticheskij stroj jazyka kla-dan v tipologicheskom kontekste rodstvennyx jazykov. Avtoreferat, kand. diss., Institute of Linguistics RAS, Moscow.
sources.note: Avtoreferat (open text, cheloveknauka.com) summarises Ch. 2 'Fonologicheskaja sistema': vowels, consonants, four level tones (ultra-high, high, low, ultra-low), and the foot (стопа) with its types and nasal/consonant harmony; 'ударение' (stress) never occurs. Says the dissertation redefines the metric foot so that it fits 'both accentual and tonal languages'. Kla-Dan variety (klad1234). Full 342-pp. dissertation not opened.

sources.note: Abstract read: measures homograph ambiguity when tone is unmarked, treating lexical and grammatical tone separately; Eastern Dan 'with its profusion of nominal and verbal minimal pairs, not to mention pronouns, case markers, predicative markers' has by far the highest written ambiguity of the three — i.e. documents the very high lexical and grammatical functional load of Eastern Dan tone; the Eastern Dan section presumably restates the 5-level + contour inventory.
